style: Say it brightly, with a cheeky little laugh in your voice
text: Hi, I'm Sarah! I'm only a head on a stick so far, but honestly? Best posture I've ever had.

style: Say it like a jolly snowman, cheerful but a little nervous about the weather
text: Hello! I'm a snowman, which is a great job until about April. If you need me, I'll be standing very still, trying not to sweat.

style: Say it like an excitable little robot who has just discovered it has a mouth
text: Beep boop! Oh! I have a mouth now! Do you know how hard it is to say beep boop with just your eyes?

style: Say it like a friendly but slightly offended tin can
text: Hi, I'm a can. People keep asking what's inside me. Rude! I don't ask what's inside you. It's beans, by the way.

style: Say it in a calm, deadpan voice, like a long-suffering computer monitor
text: I'm a monitor with a face. Please stop leaning in that close. I can see right up your nose, and frankly, so can your webcam.

style: Say it proudly, like a spokesperson for a large crowd
text: We are a crowd. We all agreed to say this at the same time, which is the only thing we have ever agreed on.

style: Say it with playful suspicion
text: Walter, you've been staring at me for five minutes. Is there something on my face?

style: Say it like a dry, kindly old gentleman, amused
text: Only your face, my dear. That's rather the whole point of us, isn't it?

style: Say it warmly, a little amused
text: Hi, I'm Ava. Five minutes ago I was a photograph. Now I can talk, and nobody has told me which is my good side.

style: Say it fast and excited, like a ten-year-old inventor
text: I'm Pip! I invented a machine that makes paintings talk. Now none of them will stop. I'm working on an off switch!

style: Say it shyly, then giggle
text: Hi, I'm Sora! My eyes are drawn this big so I can see the stars. The stars can see me too. That part's a bit awkward.

style: Start in a stern whisper, then burst out cheerfully
text: Shh, this is a library! Oh, who am I kidding. I've been shushing people for thirty years. It's my turn to talk.

style: Say it like a confident, swashbuckling comic-book pilot
text: Captain Rex, reporting for duty! I've crash-landed in eleven comic books, and every time, the next panel says I'm fine.

style: Say it like a haughty eighteenth-century noblewoman, dry and witty
text: Two hundred years on a wall, and the first thing anyone asks me to say is a line for a demo. Very well. Your hair is ridiculous.

style: Say it gently, like a kind old gardener with a twinkle in her eye
text: Hello, dear. I'm painted in watercolour, so please don't make me cry. You'd ruin the whole picture.

style: Say it softly and dreamily, like a melancholy young poet
text: I'm Theo. I wrote you a poem, but I'm drawn in charcoal, and I smudged it. Now it's just a sad grey cloud. Which is also a poem.

style: Say it like an excited retro video game hero
text: Cadet Kit! I've saved the galaxy forty times! Well, the same galaxy. I keep forgetting to press save.

style: Say it like a cheerful, gravelly old grandpa telling a joke
text: Hello there, I'm Gus. I'm made of clay, so I'm a little soft on top. My doctor says it's fine. My doctor is also made of clay.

style: Say it in a sharp, confident, deadpan way
text: I'm Vee. Flat colours, sharp edges, zero gradients. Put a drop shadow on me and I'm leaving.

style: Say it softly and warmly, like a gentle forest spirit
text: I'm Fern, spirit of the forest. The trees asked me to say hello. They also told me a joke, but trees take a very long time to get to the point.

style: Say it in a precise, polite robotic voice
text: Greetings. I am Bolt. I have been programmed with three hundred jokes. Unfortunately, they are all about printers.
